name: Possible lateral movement (hypothesis)
purpose: Connect a high-severity IDS alert to a successful sign-in from the same source address shortly afterwards.
description: Sequence rule: IDS alert (severity >= 7) followed within 15 minutes by a successful authentication from the same source address. This is a HYPOTHESIS built from two independent observations.

attack.justification: Not asserted. Remote-service techniques (e.g. T1021) are candidates for analyst review, but two correlated events do not establish one.

playbook.what: A high-severity IDS alert and then a successful sign-in were both seen from {src_ip}.
playbook.why: If the alert reflects a real exploit, the sign-in could be an attacker moving to another system. It could also be an unrelated coincidence.
playbook.howSure: Low. This links two events by address and timing only. It is a hypothesis to check, not a finding.
next: Check who normally signs in from {src_ip} and whether the account used is expected.
Compare the IDS alert destination with the sign-in destination.
Review all activity from {src_ip} in the surrounding hour.
verify: The sign-in is confirmed as expected activity or investigated further.
No further sign-ins from {src_ip} to additional hosts.
alternatives: Coincidence: an admin workstation triggers IDS noise and signs in for routine work.
NAT or shared addresses merge unrelated users.
